**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2024096)

**Proposed mechanism:** IDUA (HGNC:5315) —DISRUPTS→ Glycosaminoglycan degradation (GO:0000241); NAGLU (HGNC:7710) —DISRUPTS→ Glycosaminoglycan degradation (GO:0000241); Glycosaminoglycan degradation (GO:0000241) —DECREASES→ Undegraded glycosaminoglycans (CHEBI:17487); Undegraded glycosaminoglycans (CHEBI:17487) —LEADS_TO→ Lysosomal storage (HP:0002117); MFN2 (HGNC:16967) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial fusion and axonal transport (GO:0007008); Mitochondrial fusion and axonal transport (GO:0007008) —LEADS_TO→ Axonal degeneration (HP:0004831); Lysosomal storage (HP:0002117) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial fusion and axonal transport (GO:0007008). Loss-of-function mutations in IDUA and NAGLU impair glycosaminoglycan degradation, leading to lysosomal storage. This lysosomal dysfunction can secondarily disrupt mitochondrial function and axonal transport, contributing to the axonal degeneration seen in CMT2V, which is also directly caused by mutations in MFN2 affecting mitochondrial dynamics and axonal integrity.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that lysosomal storage in MPS I does not lead to secondary disruption of mitochondrial dynamics or axonal transport pathways, or that mutations in MFN2 do not cause any detectable lysosomal abnormalities.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of lysosomal dysfunction and its downstream effects on mitochondrial health and axonal integrity could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for both MPS I and CMT2V, potentially targeting common cellular pathways to mitigate neurodegeneration.
